The data-manager warehouse

Raw & derived tables · SF1 reference · PIT universe · stock tear sheets

Author

data-manager project

Published

August 12, 2026

Abstract. ~/.prime/agent/data_manager.db is the single local SQLite source of point-in-time market data for the quant stack: 61.7M as-traded daily price rows (stocks and funds) back to 1998, a 3.15M-row SF1 fundamentals mirror in all six reporting dimensions, the full Sharadar securities master (31,742 instruments, survivorship-free), corporate actions (670k rows incl. delistings), and a locally derived point-in-time investable universe (universe_pit, 13.5M stock-days across 7,187 trading days). This report separates the raw Sharadar bulk tables from the locally derived ones, documents every SF1 column and reporting dimension, dissects the PIT universe (market-cap bins, sector and industry coverage), gives tear sheets for a mega / mid / small cap, and reports freshness and data-quality findings. Numbers are as of the 2026-08-11 warehouse build; the PIT universe was rebuilt 2026-08-12 after a profile-carriage bug fix (see §5).

2 Raw Sharadar tables vs locally derived tables

The dataset is split by lineage, not by name. The four raw families come from executable bulk zips (.csv.zip), always fetchable again; every derived table can be wiped and rebuilt with a single CLI command and no market-data requests.

Rebuild map (all local, no API): build-piotroski / build-quarterly / build-ratios / build-universe-pit [--history] under data-manager; a from-zero warehouse rebuild is bulk-fromzero (downloads the zips once, loads, derives, builds PIT, optimizes).

The prices.adjustment contract. adjustment satisfies \(P^{\mathrm{adj}}_t = P^{\mathrm{as\text{-}traded}}_t \times \mathrm{adjustment}_t\) where \(P^{\mathrm{adj}}\) is the split- and dividend-adjusted close (Sharadar closeadj). The as-traded OHLC stored in the table is recovered from the bulk file by scaling the split-adjusted OHLC with the same-row split factor closeunadj/close; therefore close is the true as-traded price and the adjustment factor only matters for total-return series (0a78 quantifies the no-trade and adjustment-tail rows).

3 Price coverage & depth

Daily as-traded OHLCV, survivorship-free (delisted names stay in the table). The stocks-vs-funds split uses the bulk-file origin (securities_master.table).

Stocks are continuous from 1997-01 (46,263,130 rows), funds from 1997-01 (15,475,363 rows). Stock coverage runs ~8,000–9,000 quoted tickers/year from 1998 onward (delisted names included, so yearly counts are quoted securities, not survivors); fund coverage grows from a few hundred to 6,434 tickers after 2010. The 8,391-row 1997 sliver is a bulk-file edge (pre-window rows for a handful of names), consistent with the Sharadar per-ticker window cap of ~28.6y noted at migration time.

4 SF1 fundamentals: columns and reporting dimensions

The SF1 mirror is the fundamentals backbone. Every raw row carries 112 indicator fields; the table exposes 31 of them as typed columns (plus the six key fields) and keeps the full vendor row compressed in the data blob (zlib → JSON), so nothing is lost. Reporting dimensions are the key to using the mirror without look-ahead bias.

4.1 Reporting dimensions: As-Reported vs Most-Recent-Reported

Sharadar delivers fundamentals in six time dimensions — two views × three periods. The naming is AR = As-Reported, MR = Most-Recent (i.e. latest)-Reported, with suffix Y annual, Q quarterly, T trailing twelve months (TTM):

dimension view period Sharadar definition (verbatim)
ARQ As-Reported quarterly “As Reported view (AR) excludes restatements, point-in-time view with data time-indexed to the date the form 10 regulatory filing was submitted to the SEC … may include multiple observations in a quarter if more than one filing is made during the quarter” — “typically suitable for back-testing”
ARY As-Reported annual same AR semantics, annual observations
ART As-Reported TTM same AR semantics, trailing-twelve-month observations
MRQ Most-Recent-Reported quarterly “Most Recent Reported view (MR) includes restatements, time indexed to the financial/report period … presents the most recently reported data for that reporting period” — “typically suitable for assessing business performance after restatements for mergers/divestitures”
MRY Most-Recent-Reported annual same MR semantics, annual observations
MRT Most-Recent-Reported TTM same MR semantics, TTM observations

Practical rules. Use AR* for point-in-time work (backtests, PIT screens) with the row’s date as the as-of availability date — date <= D is a valid point-in-time filter and is exactly what universe_pit does for shares. Use MR* for “what do we believe today” snapshots (build-ratios uses the latest MRY row). Restatements create AR-vs-MR splits on the same report period; when a company catches up after a reporting gap, ARQ may hold several filings for one quarter.

Row-level fields (all rows, all dimensions): ticker, dimension, date (Date Key — the as-of/publishable date; for AR rows ≈ SEC filing date), calendardate (calendar date of the reporting period), reportperiod (fiscal period end), fiscalperiod (e.g. 2025-FY, 2025-Q3), lastupdated (vendor refresh timestamp), and the 112 indicators below.

105 rows × 4 columns

Notes on semantics (verified from vendor docs + live rows):

  • Scale. Every monetary field is raw as-reported units; the master’s scalemarketcap / scalerevenue columns are the Sharadar 10^scale convention but the bulk file’s SF1 rows are already unscaled (AAPL 1999 assets = 5.44B exactly).
  • FX. *usd fields are USD-normalized versions of the same line item (revenueusd, ebitusd, …); fxusd is the FX rate applied.
  • Shares. shareswa (weighted avg) and sharesbas (basic) are used for PIT market cap in universe_pit (price × shareswa, ARQ/ARY ≤ date).
  • Valuation blanks. pe1/ps1 are forward-looking (next-period); SF1 does not carry forward_pe or beta → those stay NULL in ratios (documented limitation).
  • TTM. ART/MRT rows exist (660k/737k) — TTM is a real dimension on the bulk file (the API serves 0 rows for it, another reason to use bulk).

5 PIT universe analysis

universe_pit is the locally derived investable universe — one row per (trading day, member) for 7,187 trading days (1998-01-14 → 2026-08-11). Algorithm (per ticker, no remote requests): walk its price rows keeping a rolling 20-session dollar-volume window and a pointer to the latest as-reported shares (SF1 ARQ/ARY date ≤ row date); a price row is valid when as-traded close ≥ $2, rolling avg $volume ≥ $5M with ≥ 10 sessions, and PIT mcap = close × shares ≥ $300M. Valid rows merge into runs that extend at most max_quote_age = 10 calendar days past the last fresh quote, then expand onto the global trading calendar.

2026-08-12 fix (important). The original build stored the run-start quote’s price/mcap/dvol for the whole run — a continuously trading name has one run from 1998 to today, so AAPL carried $19.75 (1998) as its 2026 profile. Membership dates were correct; the attached profile was not. Rebuilt so each member day carries the most recent valid quote ≤ that day (regression-tested; tests/test_db.py). All PIT numbers in this section use the rebuilt table.

Membership grows from 776 names (1998-01-14) to 2,435 (2026-08-11); the 2020 crash bottom holds 2,093 members (2020-03-23), and the eqrm window (2021-08-10 → 2024-12-31) holds 2,317 → 2,267.

Reading it. The universe is small-cap-heavy by count (the $300M–1B bucket holds 383 members, 15.7% of names) but mega-cap-dominated by value: the 126 names ≥ $100B (1.4% of members) hold 69.3% of the total member mcap. Raising the screen to a Russell-1000-style $5B floor keeps 1,135 names; a $1B floor keeps 2,052. The default $300M / $5M-dvol cut admits 2,435 of the 21,960 stocks in the master (11.1%) — the screen is liquidity- and data-driven, so small illiquid names and names without current SF1 shares drop out by design.

7 GICS classification coverage

classifications carries the eqrm gate: the eleven GICS labels mapped from Sharadar’s taxonomy. Coverage is a known gap — only the iShares-era universe (2,589 names) is classified, not the full 21,960-stock master; securities_master.sector/industry (Sharadar taxonomy) covers every instrument but uses non-GICS labels (e.g. Healthcare vs Health Care). The NOTES.md action item — a live GICS-map coverage check against the whole master — remains open.

Classified names: 2,589 of 21,960 stocks in the master (11.8% coverage). No NULL sectors; the five Cash and/or Derivatives rows are iShares IWV placeholders that carry no GICS sector and are excluded from the eqrm allowlist by construction.

Findings. (1) No-trade placeholder rows: 5.5% of price rows carry volume = 0 with a positive close; ~301k of them carry the 8.5×10¹⁸ overflow sentinel in adjustment (Sharadar did not populate closeadj for the row). (2) The adjustment tail is mostly mechanical: even among traded rows ~1.8% have adjustment > 100 (cumulative split+dividend rescale of long histories). As-traded close is unaffected, so returns/factor work should use close directly, applying adjustment only for total-return series, screening volume = 0 and adjustment outliers. (3) Two rows with close ≤ 0 exist (cleanup candidate).
